trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cancun
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded public beaches. day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM. Take the affordable ADO bus from the airport to the Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera) for around $10 USD instead of a taxi. Check in at Cancun Beach Resort, drop off luggage, and get oriented with the local area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest public beach access point for a relaxed first afternoon dip in the Caribbean. Walk along the beachfront boulevard to get your bearings, pick up snacks and essentials at a nearby Oxxo convenience store or Chedraui supermarket to stock up on budget-friendly drinks and snacks for the room.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Boulevard Kukulcan in the Hotel Zone. Grab dinner at one of the local taco stands or a casual restaurant away from the main tourist strip. Settle in early to rest after travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing — airport Oxxo or a quick café bite (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Pick up street tacos or a torta from a local taqueria near the hotel zone (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: El Fish Fritanga or a local cocina económica (budget Mexican diner) near the hotel zone — rice, beans, and grilled fish plate (~$8-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep it light. Exchange a small amount of currency or use ATMs at the airport for pesos. Avoid airport taxis; the ADO bus is far cheaper. Stock up on water and snacks at Chedraui or Walmart nearby to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Playa Delfines — one of Cancun's most iconic FREE public beaches. Arrive early (around 8:30–9:00 AM) to grab a prime spot before it gets busy. Enjoy the turquoise waters, soft white sand, and the famous Cancun sign for photos. Bring snacks and water from your hotel to save money.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at Playa Delfines or explore the beach on foot. Rent a beach umbrella if needed (very affordable at public beaches, ~$5 USD). Take a refreshing swim in the calm Caribbean waters. Walk north along the shoreline to explore the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the hotel to freshen up. Walk or take a local bus (Route 1 — only ~$0.80 USD) to downtown Cancun (El Centro) for a more authentic and budget-friendly dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast using snacks/fruit bought at the supermarket in your room (~$2-3 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the hotel or grab elotes (grilled corn), fresh fruit cups, and agua frescas from vendors near Playa Delfines (~$3-5 USD)
meals.dinner: Tacos Rigo or Mercado 28 in downtown Cancun — try cochinita pibil tacos or fresh ceviche tostadas (~$6-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is completely free to access and is one of the best beaches in Cancun. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, plenty of water, and a beach towel. The local Route 1 bus runs the entire Hotel Zone and is the most budget-friendly transport option at under $1 USD per ride.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Punta Nizuc Reef — head to the southern tip of the Hotel Zone to explore the vibrant coral reef at Punta Nizuc, part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef system. Rent snorkel gear on-site (~$10-15 USD) or bring your own if you packed it. The reef is accessible directly from the beach, making it one of the most affordable snorkeling spots in Cancun.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, relax on the beach at Punta Nizuc. The area is less crowded than the main Hotel Zone beaches. Explore the shallow reef areas and look for tropical fish, sea turtles, and colorful coral formations. Take the local bus back toward the hotel zone in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the free public Playa Langosta or Playa Tortugas beach area for a sunset walk. These beaches have a lively local atmosphere in the evenings with vendors and families.

meals.breakfast: Grab a hearty breakfast at a downtown Cancun comedor (local diner) — eggs, beans, tortillas, and coffee (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Beachside fresh ceviche or fish tacos from a local vendor near Punta Nizuc (~$5-8 USD)
meals.dinner: La Habichuela Downtown or a local seafood restaurant in El Centro — try the budget-friendly set menu (menú del día) which includes soup, main dish, and drink (~$8-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Punta Nizuc is best visited in the morning when the water is calmest and clearest. Wear reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem. The snorkeling here is genuinely world-class and costs a fraction of organized tours. Bring an underwater camera or a waterproof phone case for photos.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Isla Mujeres via the public ferry from Puerto Juárez (not the more expensive Hotel Zone ferry). The ferry costs around $5-7 USD each way. Arrive on the island and rent a golf cart (~$30-40 USD for a few hours split between travel companions) or explore by walking and renting a bicycle (~$8-10 USD) to see the entire small island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Playa Norte on Isla Mujeres — consistently ranked one of the most beautiful beaches in the Caribbean. The water is incredibly calm, shallow, and crystal clear. Swim, snorkel, and relax on this stunning free public beach. Explore the colorful downtown streets and browse local artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the ferry back to Cancun before sunset (last ferries run around 8:00-9:00 PM). Grab dinner back in the Hotel Zone or downtown Cancun.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel or a pan dulce (sweet bread) and café de olla from a local bakery near the ferry terminal (~$2-4 USD)
meals.lunch: Fresh fish tacos or a lobster taco (surprisingly affordable on the island) at a local restaurant on Isla Mujeres (~$8-12 USD)
meals.dinner: Taqueria Los Paisanos or a local spot in downtown Cancun upon return — grilled chicken or beef tacos with salsa (~$6-9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Use the Puerto Juárez ferry terminal instead of the Playa Caracol or Hotel Zone ferry docks — it is significantly cheaper. The ride takes about 20 minutes. Isla Mujeres is very walkable in the town center. Bring cash as some smaller establishments may not accept cards. This is one of the best value day trips from Cancun.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a different section of Cancun's Hotel Zone beach — try Playa Chac Mool or Playa Marlin, both free public beaches with calmer waters and beautiful scenery. Arrive early for the best experience. Bring your snorkel gear for some casual reef exploration along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Zona Arqueológica El Rey — ancient Mayan ruins located right in the Hotel Zone near the lagoon side. Admission is very affordable (~$3-4 USD). Walk among the ruins and learn about the Mayan history of the area. Afterward, visit the Mercado de Artesanías (crafts market) in downtown Cancun to browse souvenirs at much lower prices than Hotel Zone shops.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset from the beachfront. Head to Parque de las Palapas in downtown Cancun — a lively free public square with street food vendors, live music on weekends, and a very local authentic atmosphere perfect for a budget evening out.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie and tamales from a street vendor near the hotel zone (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch on the beach — pick up fresh fruit, chips, guacamole, and drinks from a nearby Oxxo or market (~$5-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food at Parque de las Palapas — try marquesitas (crispy crepes with cheese and fillings), elotes, and fresh juices (~$4-7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: El Rey Ruins are a hidden gem that most tourists skip — they offer a genuine glimpse into Mayan history without the crowds or high prices of Chichen Itza. Parque de las Palapas is the heart of local Cancun life and is completely free. Friday evenings often have live music and a very festive atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning beach session — return to your favorite beach from the trip (Playa Delfines recommended for a farewell swim). Enjoy the Caribbean one last time, take final photos, and soak up the sun. Pack up your belongings at the hotel and check out, storing luggage at the front desk if your flight is later.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Mercado 28 in downtown Cancun — the best and most affordable place to buy authentic Mexican crafts, hammocks, textiles, and gifts. Practice bargaining for better prices. Grab a final authentic Mexican meal before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Take the ADO bus from the Hotel Zone back to Cancun International Airport (~$10 USD). Arrive at least 2-3 hours before your departure flight. Reflect on an amazing budget-friendly Cancun adventure!

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a final visit to a local comedor for a classic Mexican breakfast of chilaquiles or huevos rancheros (~$5-7 USD)
meals.lunch: Final lunch at Mercado 28 — try the pozole, sopa de lima, or fresh seafood tostadas from the market food stalls (~$6-10 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport snack or meal if flight timing allows — or grab a torta and agua fresca to go from a downtown spot before heading to the airport (~$4-6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — ask the hotel to store your bags if you need the afternoon free. The ADO bus to the airport is the most cost-effective option. Arrive at the airport early as Cancun International can get busy, especially on weekends. Keep some pesos for any last-minute airport purchases or tips.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Cancun Beach Resort. Check-in, freshen up, and get oriented with the hotel amenities and surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to the hotel beach or nearest public beach stretch for a relaxed first afternoon. Take a leisurely walk along the Hotel Zone shoreline, dip your toes in the Caribbean, and decompress from travel. Pick up any essentials at a nearby convenience store or pharmacy.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Boulevard Kukulcan and explore the Hotel Zone at night. Enjoy a welcome dinner at a mid-range beachfront restaurant near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing
meals.lunch: La Habichuela Downtown or a casual taqueria near the resort upon arrival — budget around $10–15 USD
meals.dinner: El Fish Fritanga or Lorenzillo's — fresh seafood with ocean views, mid-range pricing around $20–30 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11:00 AM, keep Day 1 light and low-key. Allow 1–1.5 hours for airport formalities and transfer. No pre-booked morning activities needed. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance in case early check-in is required.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a full morning at Playa Delfines Beach Day — one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded public beaches. Arrive early (around 9:00 AM) to secure a good spot. Swim in the turquoise Caribbean waters, relax on the white sand, and take in the famous Cancun sign photo opportunity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at Playa Delfines or walk the surrounding area. Rent a beach chair and umbrella if needed. Around 2:00 PM, head back toward the Hotel Zone and visit Mercado 28 for local crafts, souvenirs, and authentic Mexican street food.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset walk along the Hotel Zone lagoon side. Wind down with dinner at a mid-range local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel restaurant or a nearby café — eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee, around $8–12 USD
meals.lunch: Street tacos or a casual eatery near Mercado 28 — budget around $8–12 USD
meals.dinner: La Parrilla Cancun — popular Mexican grill with live music and great value, around $15–25 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a public beach with free access. Bring sunscreen, water, and cash for vendors. The beach can have stronger waves — check flags before swimming. Taxis or the R-1 bus route are affordable ways to reach Playa Delfines from the Hotel Zone.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Isla Mujeres Catamaran Day Trip — depart from Puerto Juárez or the Hotel Zone marina around 9:00–10:00 AM. Sail on a catamaran to the stunning Isla Mujeres, enjoying open bar and snacks on board. Snorkel in crystal-clear Caribbean waters teeming with colorful marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Isla Mujeres and explore the charming island on foot or by golf cart rental. Visit the colorful streets, Playa Norte (one of Mexico's most beautiful beaches), and browse local artisan shops. Enjoy lunch on the island.
day_by_day.evening: Return catamaran trip back to Cancun (usually around 4:00–5:00 PM). Rest at the hotel, then head out for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh ceviche and grilled fish at a beachside restaurant on Isla Mujeres — around $12–18 USD
meals.dinner: Sunset Grill or Ty-Coz near the Hotel Zone — casual and affordable, around $15–20 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Isla Mujeres catamaran day trip in advance — many operators offer pick-up from Hotel Zone hotels. Typical cost is $55–80 USD per person including snorkeling gear, open bar, and snacks. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a light cover-up, and a waterproof bag. Golf cart rental on Isla Mujeres costs around $40–50 USD for a couple of hours.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Punta Nizuc Reef — head to the southern tip of the Hotel Zone to explore the vibrant coral reef at Punta Nizuc, part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef system. Rent snorkeling gear on-site or bring your own. Arrive around 9:00 AM for calmer waters and better visibility.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, relax on the nearby beach at Punta Nizuc or visit Club Med's public beach access area. In the mid-afternoon, return to the hotel for a rest, then explore the Kukulcan Plaza mall for shopping, air conditioning, and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely evening dinner with a view of the lagoon or Caribbean Sea.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — full buffet if available, or nearby café
meals.lunch: Casual beachside palapa restaurant near Punta Nizuc — grilled fish tacos and fresh juice, around $10–15 USD
meals.dinner: Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar or Labná — upscale yet mid-range Yucatecan cuisine, around $25–35 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Punta Nizuc reef snorkeling gear rental typically costs $10–20 USD. Water shoes are recommended as the reef entry can be rocky. Visibility is best in the morning. Avoid touching or standing on coral. The area is accessible by taxi from the Hotel Zone (about 10–15 minutes).

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion: Cenote Dos Ojos Swimming and Snorkeling near Tulum (about 1.5–2 hours from Cancun). Depart by 8:00 AM via organized tour or rental car. Swim and snorkel through the breathtaking underground cave system with crystal-clear freshwater and dramatic stalactites.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cenote visit, stop in Tulum town or Tulum beach for lunch and a brief explore of the area. Optionally visit the Tulum archaeological ruins overlooking the Caribbean Sea (about 30 minutes from Dos Ojos). Begin the return drive to Cancun by 4:00–5:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Cancun by early evening. Relax at the resort, enjoy the hotel pool or beach, and have a low-key dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast at the hotel or a convenience stop on the road — fruit, pastries, coffee
meals.lunch: Hartwood or a casual taqueria in Tulum town — fresh, local ingredients, around $12–20 USD
meals.dinner: Room service or hotel restaurant for a relaxed night in — around $15–25 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book the Cenote Dos Ojos tour in advance — organized day trips from Cancun typically cost $60–100 USD per person including transport and guide. If self-driving, entrance to Dos Ojos is around $20–25 USD per person. Bring water shoes, a change of clothes, and a dry bag. Avoid wearing sunscreen before entering the cenote to protect the ecosystem. This is a long day — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cancun — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel and take one last swim in the Caribbean. Pack up, check out, and store luggage with the hotel concierge if needed. Take a final stroll along the beach to soak in the views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the early afternoon at a nearby beach or pool area. If time allows, pick up any last-minute souvenirs at Mercado 28 or a local shop. Grab a light lunch before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Beach Bonfire and Seafood Dinner — if your departure allows, end the trip with this magical guided sunset experience on a quieter stretch of beach, featuring a bonfire, fresh seafood dinner, and the sound of the Caribbean waves as a perfect farewell to Cancun.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — treat yourself on the last morning, around $12–18 USD
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside café or taqueria — fish tacos and agua fresca, around $8–12 USD
meals.dinner: Sunset Beach Bonfire and Seafood Dinner experience — typically $45–70 USD per person including food and guided experience

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel (usually 12:00 PM noon). The Sunset Beach Bonfire experience typically starts around 5:00–6:00 PM — book in advance and confirm it doesn't conflict with your departure flight. If flying out in the evening, allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. A wonderful, memorable way to close out the trip!

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Cancun Beach Resort. Check-in, unpack, and settle into your premium suite overlooking the Caribbean. Take a leisurely stroll along the resort's private beach to acclimate to the stunning surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort's private beach and pool area. Enjoy complimentary welcome cocktails, lounge on premium beach chairs, and take your first dip in the turquoise Caribbean waters. Request a beachside cabana for the ultimate relaxation experience.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant. Savor fresh local seafood and regional Mexican cuisine while watching the sunset over the Caribbean Sea.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light bite at the airport before arrival
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort's beach club — fresh ceviche, guacamole, and tropical fruit platters with artisan cocktails
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — recommended: grilled Caribbean lobster, Yucatecan-spiced fish, and a curated mezcal tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Given the 11:00 AM arrival, allow 60–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and the private transfer to the resort. No off-site activities are scheduled on Day 1 to allow for smooth settling in. Confirm cabana reservation with the concierge upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Playa Delfines Beach Day — After a leisurely breakfast, head to one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded public beaches, Playa Delfines. Arrive early to claim a prime spot. Enjoy the natural beauty, powerful waves, and panoramic views of the Hotel Zone. Bring premium beach gear from the resort (towels, umbrellas, cooler).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Playa Delfines or explore the surrounding area. Take a scenic walk along the shoreline, try bodyboarding in the surf, or simply relax with a good book. Return to the resort mid-afternoon for a spa treatment — book a 90-minute couples' massage or a traditional Mayan herbal body wrap at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Elegant dinner at a top-rated restaurant in the Hotel Zone, followed by a sunset cocktail on the resort's rooftop terrace or beach bar.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet buffet breakfast at the resort — fresh tropical fruits, made-to-order eggs, smoked salmon, artisan pastries, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Chic beachside lunch at a nearby beach club near Playa Delfines — grilled fish tacos, shrimp aguachile, and ice-cold craft beers or agua frescas
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Habichuela Sunset or a comparable upscale Cancun restaurant — try the cocobichuela (lobster and shrimp in a tropical curry sauce served in a coconut)

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a public beach with no entry fee, but parking can fill up. Arrange a private driver or taxi through the resort concierge for convenience. Apply high-SPF reef-safe sunscreen. Book the spa treatment at least one day in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Isla Mujeres Catamaran Day Trip — Depart from Puerto Juárez or the Hotel Zone marina on a premium private or small-group catamaran. Sail across the turquoise waters of the Caribbean to the charming island of Isla Mujeres. Enjoy snorkeling in crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Isla Mujeres and explore the colorful downtown area. Rent a golf cart to tour the island at your own pace, visiting Punta Sur (the southernmost tip of Mexico), the scenic cliffs, and the beautiful Playa Norte — consistently rated one of the best beaches in the Caribbean. Swim in the calm, shallow turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by catamaran as the sun begins to set — enjoy champagne and snacks on the return sail. Back at the resort, freshen up and enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh fruit, yogurt parfait, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachfront restaurant on Isla Mujeres — grilled whole fish, lobster tacos, and chilled white wine or tropical cocktails at Playa Norte
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort or a nearby fine-dining spot — try Hartwood Tulum-style wood-fire cuisine or a premium sushi and ceviche bar in the Hotel Zone

day_by_day.notes: Book a private catamaran charter for the most luxurious experience — the resort concierge can arrange this. The trip to Isla Mujeres takes approximately 20–30 minutes by ferry or catamaran. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a light cover-up, and cash for the island. Golf cart rentals on the island cost approximately $40–60 USD for a few hours.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Punta Nizuc Reef — Join a guided premium snorkeling excursion to Punta Nizuc, located at the southern tip of the Hotel Zone and part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef system — the second largest coral reef in the world. Explore vibrant coral formations, sea fans, and an abundance of tropical marine life in warm, clear Caribbean waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a relaxed afternoon. Indulge in a private poolside cabana with personalized butler service. Enjoy premium cocktails, chilled towels, and fresh fruit. Alternatively, take a paddleboard or kayak lesson offered by the resort's water sports center.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a stylish rooftop bar in the Hotel Zone, followed by a premium dinner at one of Cancun's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort — eggs Benedict with smoked marlin, avocado toast, fresh-pressed juices, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Light post-snorkel lunch at the resort's beach club or a nearby casual upscale spot — fish tacos, shrimp ceviche tostadas, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Dinner at Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar or a comparable luxury restaurant — prime cuts, fresh oysters, and an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Punta Nizuc is accessible by boat from the Hotel Zone — the resort concierge can arrange a guided snorkeling tour with professional equipment included. The reef is a protected area, so only reef-safe sunscreen is permitted. Water visibility is typically excellent in March. Book the cabana for the afternoon at least the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Cenote Dos Ojos Swimming and Snorkeling — Embark on a premium full-day excursion to the breathtaking Dos Ojos cenote system near Tulum (approximately 2 hours from Cancun). Arrive early with a private guide to beat the crowds. Swim and snorkel through hauntingly beautiful underground cave systems with crystal-clear freshwater, dramatic stalactites and stalagmites, and ethereal light rays filtering through the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cenote experience, stop in Tulum town or the Tulum Hotel Zone for lunch and exploration. Visit the iconic Tulum Ruins overlooking the Caribbean Sea for a brief cultural and historical experience, or relax at one of Tulum's bohemian-chic beach clubs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by private transfer. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a relaxed, indulgent evening — perhaps a private in-room dining experience on your balcony overlooking the sea, or a nightcap at the resort's beach bar.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — grab-and-go options including protein-rich bites, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch in Tulum at Hartwood, Gitano, or a comparable high-end jungle or beach restaurant — wood-fired dishes, fresh local ingredients, and craft cocktails
meals.dinner: Private in-room or balcony dining at the resort — curated 4-course menu with wine pairing delivered by the butler service, featuring fresh lobster, local cheeses, and a decadent dessert

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Dos Ojos cenote is approximately 2 hours each way — arrange a private luxury van or SUV with a professional driver through the resort. Bring a waterproof camera or GoPro for stunning underwater photos. Wear a swimsuit under your clothes and bring a change of clothes for after. The cenote water is cool and refreshing (around 77°F/25°C year-round). Life jackets and snorkel gear are typically provided on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — sleep in and enjoy a slow, luxurious breakfast at the resort. Take one last swim in the Caribbean Sea from the resort's private beach. Pack and prepare for departure, storing luggage with the concierge if needed for a late checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sunset Beach Bonfire and Seafood Dinner Experience — For a magical farewell, arrange the guided Sunset Beach Bonfire and Seafood Dinner on a quieter, more secluded stretch of beach. This curated experience features a private bonfire, premium fresh seafood grilled tableside, chilled champagne, and a stunning Caribbean sunset as your backdrop — the perfect send-off for a luxury Cancun trip.
day_by_day.evening: Conclude the bonfire dinner experience and transfer back to the resort or directly to Cancun International Airport depending on your departure flight schedule. Enjoy final cocktails at the resort bar and reflect on an unforgettable week in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the resort — full à la carte gourmet spread with champagne mimosas, eggs any style, smoked fish, tropical fruits, and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Light poolside or beach lunch at the resort — fresh salads, ceviche, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: The Sunset Beach Bonfire and Seafood Dinner experience — whole grilled lobster, jumbo shrimp skewers, fresh fish, roasted corn and vegetables, artisan bread, and chilled champagne by the fire

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the Sunset Beach Bonfire and Seafood Dinner booking with the resort concierge at least 2–3 days in advance as this is a guided, curated experience that requires preparation. Request late checkout from the resort to maximize your final day. If your return flight is late evening, you can store luggage at the front desk and enjoy the beach until transfer time. Arrange airport transfer through the resort for a seamless, premium departure experience.

query: Cancun beach resort, $3000 couple, 6 days, March 2027, from Dallas
